I actually made this guys metal foundry about a month ago. I haven't used it yet, because I'm waiting for my crucible to come in. If you make the foundry, then I wouldn't recommend using the steel extinguisher seeing as aluminum becomes corrosive to steel at certain temperatures. Instead, use a ceramic graphic crucible. He actually mentions it in an AMA over there.

Edit: He got everything from Home Depot. I couldn't find hardly anything that he used in the foundry vid at Lowe's. Everything was at HD and the bigmouth bucket can only be bought online.
How much for the crucible? Is the crucible a consumable item or does it last a long time?

The price can change drastically depending on how big you want your crucible to be. The one needed for his foundry will probably cost $20 - $40. The crucible should last a very long time. If you end up looking for a ceramic graphite crucible, you can search either those three terms or substitute "ceramic" for "clay". They mean the same thing, but some people label it differently. I know amazon has a few.

Make sure you get proper gloves and tongs as well. Random work gloves won't cut it and if you use crappy tongs, then be prepared to drop the crucible when it's full of molten metal. That's obviously not something you want to happen.
